copy.blurb:
The model fancies Australia more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Paraguay. +9.3pp is a substantive gap; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Public Elo rates Australia 10 points higher than the other side (Paraguay 1730, Australia 1740). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Paraguay to win at 34%, the draw at 29%, and Australia to win at 36%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Australia sits at 36% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Paraguay to win at 44%, the draw at 30%, and Australia to win at 27%. The Australia side trades at 27% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +270. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 36%, +9.3pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Australia side that lower bound is 31% — +4.3pp clear of the market's 27%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

This number will move. The confirmed starting eleven, fitness news, weather at the venue, and any tournament suspension carried in from previous matches all feed back into the prior. With kickoff 31 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A wide Pick can collapse into a Pass if news moves enough of the read. Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades and does not recommend a wager.
drivers: Pre-match Elo gives Australia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +9.3pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Australia side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The away side reads stronger to the model than to the market. Our Elo prior puts Australia at 36%; Polymarket prices that side at 27%. The +9.3pp gap calls a Pick.
copy.title: Paraguay v Australia · the model leans Australia
